result.summary: Splits the `tx_mempool_block_doublespend` unit test into four independent test cases using a shared fixture. It also modifies the two spend transactions to use different output amounts so they have distinct transaction hashes, ensuring they are genuine conflicts.
result.problem: The four subtests previously shared chain and mempool state, requiring manual mempool removal between cases. Furthermore, identical outputs and deterministic signing meant the two transactions were identical; in the final test case, the mempool transaction was evicted because it was mined rather than because it was conflicted out by the block transaction.
evidence: Commit 0d98c438eb: 'Both spends were built identically and signed with deterministic nonces, so they were the same transaction rather than a double-spend. In the last case, the mempool transaction was therefore removed because it was mined, not because it conflicted with the block.'
result.card: Splits the tx_mempool_block_doublespend unit test into four independent test cases with fresh chain and mempool state. It updates the spend transactions to use different output values so they produce distinct txids and genuinely conflict with each other. Previously, deterministic signing on identical spends caused the mempool transaction in the final test case to be removed because it was mined rather than because it conflicted with a block transaction. The change is isolated strictly to unit test code.

risk.why: A bug would only cause unit test failures or false test passes, with no impact on production node execution.
